The [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") was confirmed to have reached [South America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_America "South America") on 26 February 2020 when Brazil confirmed a case in [São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Paulo "São Paulo").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-2) By 3 April, all countries and territories in South America had recorded at least one case.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-Stuff/Fairfax-3)

On 13 May 2020, it was reported that Latin America and the [Caribbean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean "Caribbean") had reported over 400,000 cases of COVID-19 infection with, 23,091 deaths. On 22 May 2020, citing the rapid increase of [infections in Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil "COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil"), the [World Health Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Health_Organization "World Health Organization") declared South America the epicentre of the pandemic.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-5)

As of 12 January 2023, South America had recorded 67,331,547 confirmed cases and 1,344,031 deaths from COVID-19. Due to a shortage of testing and medical facilities, it is believed that the outbreak is far larger than the official numbers show.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-6)

### Argentina

[![Image 27](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/75/COVID-19_Pandemic_Cases_in_Argentina_by_number_by_province.svg/250px-COVID-19_Pandemic_Cases_in_Argentina_by_number_by_province.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:COVID-19_Pandemic_Cases_in_Argentina_by_number_by_province.svg)

COVID-19 pandemic cases in Argentina

This section is an excerpt from [COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Argentina "COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina").[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=COVID-19_pandemic_in_Argentina&action=edit)]

The [COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Argentina "COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina") is part of the [worldwide pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") of coronavirus disease 2019 ([COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19")) caused by [severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Severe_acute_respiratory_syndrome_coronavirus_2 "Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2") (SARS-CoV-2). As of 18 September 2026, a total of 10,119,840 people were confirmed to have been infected, and 130,859 people were known to have died because of the virus.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-36)

On 3 March 2020, the virus was confirmed to have spread to [Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentina "Argentina").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-37)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Argentina_InfobaePrimer-38)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-39)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-40) On 7 March 2020, the [Ministry of Health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Health_(Argentina) "Ministry of Health (Argentina)") confirmed the country's first documented death, a 64-year-old man who had travelled to Paris, France, who also had other health conditions; the case was only confirmed as positive after the patient's demise.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Argentina_argentina.1-41)

On 19 March 2020, a nationwide lockdown was established in Argentina.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Argentina_quarantine-42)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Argentina_lockdown-43) The lockdown was lifted throughout all the country, excepting the [Greater Buenos Aires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Buenos_Aires "Greater Buenos Aires") urban area (where 31.9% of the country's population live),[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-44) on 10 May, with Greater Buenos Aires locked down until 17 July, where the lockdown was due to be gradually loosened in several stages to lead to the return to normality;[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Argentina_lockdown-end-17jul-45) restrictions were extended several times until 8 November 2020.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Argentina_lockdown-end-46) During the second wave, another nationwide lockdown took place from 22 to 31 May 2021.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Argentina_lockdown-may-21-47)

Responses to the outbreak have included [restrictions on commerce and movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stay-at-home_order "Stay-at-home order"), closure of borders, and the closure of schools and educational institutions.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Argentina_15Mar-sus-48) Clusters of infections and deaths have occurred in [nursing homes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nursing_home "Nursing home"), prisons and other detention centers, and urban areas.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-49)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-50) The number of tests increased over time, although there were some concerns as there was less testing than in other countries of the region such as Chile and Peru.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Argentina_tests-region-51) Even so, the government's responses to the pandemic were among the best received by the population in the region during the early stages of the pandemic.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Argentina_reception-LatAm-52)

### Bolivia

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Bolivia")]

This section is an excerpt from [COVID-19 pandemic in Bolivia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Bolivia "COVID-19 pandemic in Bolivia").[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=COVID-19_pandemic_in_Bolivia&action=edit)]

The [COVID-19 pandemic in Bolivia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Bolivia "COVID-19 pandemic in Bolivia") was a part of the [worldwide pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") of [coronavirus disease 2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19") (COVID-19) caused by [severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Severe_acute_respiratory_syndrome_coronavirus_2 "Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2") (SARS-CoV-2). The virus was confirmed to have spread to [Bolivia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolivia "Bolivia") on 10 March 2020, when its first two cases were confirmed in the departments of [Oruro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oruro_Department "Oruro Department") and [Santa Cruz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Cruz_Department_(Bolivia) "Santa Cruz Department (Bolivia)").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-53)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-54)

On 12 March, Bolivia suspended all public school sessions until 31 March, as well as all commercial flights to and from Europe indefinitely. They also prohibited large-scale public gatherings of more than 1,000 people.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-55)

### Brazil

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Brazil")]

This section is an excerpt from [COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil "COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil").[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil&action=edit)]

The [COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil "COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil") has resulted in 38,050,567[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-Template:COVID-19_data-56) confirmed cases of [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19") and 704,066[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-Template:COVID-19_data-56) deaths. The virus was confirmed to have spread to [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil "Brazil") on 25 February 2020,[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-57) when a man from [São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Paulo "São Paulo") who had traveled to [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy "Italy")[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-58) tested positive for the virus. The disease had spread to every [federative unit of Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federative_units_of_Brazil "Federative units of Brazil") by 21 March. On 19 June 2020, the country reported its one millionth case and nearly 49,000 reported deaths.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-59)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-60) One estimate of [under-reporting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Under-reporting#Disease "Under-reporting") was 22.62% of total reported COVID-19 mortality in 2020.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-61)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-62)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-63)

The [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") triggered a variety of responses from federal, state and local governments, having an impact on politics, education, the environment,[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil_AmazonABC-64) and the economy. On 27 March 2020 Brazil announced a temporary ban on foreign air travelers[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-65) and most state governors have imposed quarantines to prevent the spread of the virus.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-66) President [Jair Bolsonaro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jair_Bolsonaro "Jair Bolsonaro") perpetuated [conspiracy theories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_misinformation "COVID-19 misinformation") surrounding COVID-19 treatments[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil_:7-67) and its origins,[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil_:8-68) and was accused of downplaying effective mitigations and pursuing a strategy of [herd immunity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herd_immunity "Herd immunity").[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil_:9-69) In October 2021, a congressional panel recommended criminal charges against the president for his handling of the pandemic, including [crimes against humanity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crimes_against_humanity "Crimes against humanity").[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil_:9-69)

As of 18 September 2026, Brazil, with 38,050,567[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-Template:COVID-19_data-56) confirmed cases and 704,066[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-Template:COVID-19_data-56) deaths, has the third-highest number of confirmed cases and second-highest death toll from COVID-19 in the world, behind only [those of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_the_United_States "COVID-19 pandemic in the United States") and [of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_India "COVID-19 pandemic in India").

### Chile

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Chile")]

This section is an excerpt from [COVID-19 pandemic in Chile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Chile "COVID-19 pandemic in Chile").[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=COVID-19_pandemic_in_Chile&action=edit)]

The [worldwide pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") of coronavirus disease 2019 ([COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19")) caused by [severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SARS-CoV-2 "SARS-CoV-2") (SARS-CoV-2) severely affected [Chile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chile "Chile"). The virus was confirmed to have reached Chile on 3 March 2020.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Chile_First_Case-70) Initial cases had been imported from Southeast Asia and Europe, and expanded into a large number of untraceable infections, placing the country within phase 4 of the pandemic as defined by the [World Health Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Health_Organization "World Health Organization"), with over 1,000 confirmed cases by 25 March 2020.

The cases were concentrated in the [Santiago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santiago "Santiago") metropolitan area, with outbreaks in other regions in the country. No national [lockdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lockdown "Lockdown") was established in Chile, unlike [in neighboring Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Argentina "COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina") and [Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Peru "COVID-19 pandemic in Peru"), although a night [curfew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curfew "Curfew") was implemented throughout the country. Quarantines were established locally in different cities and neighborhoods. However, in May 2020 the whole city of Santiago was put under mandatory quarantine due to an increase of cases, and similar situations were extended to most of the largest cities in Chile.

Considering its population, by June 2020 Chile had one of the worst outbreaks in the world.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-71) Initially, the number of fatalities reported was lower than in other countries in South America, even those with fewer cases. However, in May 2020, the number of cases and deaths increased rapidly, while several sources reported [excess deaths](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mortality_displacement "Mortality displacement") not officially attributed to COVID-19, which were not counted.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Chile_excess_deaths_nyt-72)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-73) By June 2020, the government confirmed thousands of additional deaths due to COVID-19, including suspected cases where [PCR tests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_testing "COVID-19 testing") were not available.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Chile_sospechosos-74) The pandemic reached a peak on 13 June with 195 daily confirmed deaths and nearly 7,000 positive cases.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Chile_Govt_Report-75) By July 2020, 10,000 people had died, and Chile had the sixth largest number of cases in the world.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Chile_epidem5jul-76)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-77) In the following weeks, the number of daily cases and deaths started to decrease slowly, although some local outbreaks appeared. The number of cases increased later in the year, and by March 2021 the number of daily cases had exceeded those in the initial wave.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Chile_:1-78)

Chile became one of the first countries to start a nationwide program to [vaccinate against COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_vaccine "COVID-19 vaccine"). On 24 December 2020, the first batch of vaccines arrived in the country to inoculate mainly health workers.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Chile_:2-79) With larger batches of vaccines (mainly [Sinovac's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinovac_Biotech "Sinovac Biotech")[CoronaVac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CoronaVac "CoronaVac")) arriving from February 2021, Chile became one of the fastest countries in the world to inoculate their population: by March 2021 a quarter of the population had received at least one dose. This fast response was due to signing contracts with multiple providers, a strong public immunization program, and little [anti-vaccine sentiment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-vaccine_sentiment "Anti-vaccine sentiment").[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-80) Despite the success of the vaccination program the number of cases increased, which has been attributed to early relaxation of restrictions and a false sense of security.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-81)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-82)[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-83)

With more than 92,000 cases and 2,500 deaths per million inhabitants,[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Chile_Govt_Report-75) the [impact of the pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_of_the_COVID-19_pandemic "Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic") has been great in the South American country. In March 2020, when the first cases of COVID-19 were reported, the country was still facing [protests and riots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%932022_Chilean_protests "2019–2022 Chilean protests")[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-eyes-85) that had begun in October 2019, and the pandemic affected the scheduled [2020 Chilean constitutional referendum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Chilean_constitutional_referendum "2020 Chilean constitutional referendum"), which was rescheduled and held later in the year. Partial lockdowns and quarantines were established in the first months, [hitting the economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_impact_of_the_COVID-19_pandemic "Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic") of the country. By April 2020, unemployment had reached 9%, a ten-year high.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-86)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-87) A wave of protests sparked in late May, mainly in Santiago, due to food shortages in certain sectors of the population.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-88) The Chilean GDP shrank by a 5.8% in 2020, the largest recession in 40 years in the country.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-89) Chile is the only country in the world with entry procedures such as requiring homologation of vaccines to travel to.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-90)

### Colombia

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Colombia")]

This section is an excerpt from [COVID-19 pandemic in Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Colombia "COVID-19 pandemic in Colombia").[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=COVID-19_pandemic_in_Colombia&action=edit)]

The [COVID-19 pandemic in Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Colombia "COVID-19 pandemic in Colombia") was a part of the [pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") of [coronavirus disease 2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19") (COVID-19) caused by [severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Severe_acute_respiratory_syndrome_coronavirus_2 "Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2") (SARS-CoV-2). The virus was confirmed to have reached [Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia "Colombia") on 6 March 2020.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Colombia_reuters6march-91)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-92)

Up to January 2022, four waves affected Colombia: Infections and deaths peaked in August 2020, again in January 2021 following the Christmas holidays, reached new highs between April and June 2021, and a fourth wave was confirmed in late December 2021 following the arrival of the [Omicron variant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SARS-CoV-2_Omicron_variant "SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant") of SARS-CoV-2.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-93)

"Confirmed COVID-19" was the primary cause of death in Colombia in 2020, where the virus caused over 50,000 fatalities by the end of the calendar year. An additional 13,000 deaths in Colombia that year were suspected to be caused by COVID-19, making "suspected COVID-19" the third most common cause of death.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-94) The "confirmed COVID-19" death toll doubled during the first half of 2021, reaching 100,000 before the end of June (including all deaths from the beginning of the pandemic).[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-95)

### Ecuador

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Ecuador")]

Main article: [COVID-19 pandemic in Ecuador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Ecuador "COVID-19 pandemic in Ecuador")

[![Image 28](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0a/COVID-19_Outbreak_Cases_in_Ecuador.svg/250px-COVID-19_Outbreak_Cases_in_Ecuador.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:COVID-19_Outbreak_Cases_in_Ecuador.svg)

Confirmed COVID-19 cases in Ecuador

On 29 February 2020, the [Minister of Health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_minister "Health minister") in Ecuador, Catalina Andramuño, confirmed the first case of the virus in the country.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-ecuador.1-96) The person, an elderly woman, was an Ecuadorian citizen residing in Spain who had arrived to Guayaquil on 14 February without showing symptoms. She fell ill and was hospitalized, where she was diagnosed with COVID.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-ecuador.1-96)

On 1 March 2020, Andramuño announced that five new cases of coronavirus have been confirmed in Ecuador.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-97)

As of 31 March 2020, there have been 2240 confirmed cases, plus 75 deaths linked to COVID-19. The Health Ministry also reported 61 deaths probably related to COVID-19.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-98)

Ecuador was described in April 2020 as emerging as the "epicentre" of the pandemic in Latin America.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-Stuff/Fairfax-3) The [Guayas Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guayas_Province "Guayas Province") was particularly strongly affected, with thousand of excess deaths reported compared to the figure for a normal period.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-bbc_ecuador-99) It was reported on 17 April 2020 that 10,939 people had died in six weeks since the start of March in the [Guayas Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guayas_Province "Guayas Province"), compared to a normal figure of 3,000 for the province.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-collyns-100)

### Peru

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Peru")]

This section is an excerpt from [COVID-19 pandemic in Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Peru "COVID-19 pandemic in Peru").[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=COVID-19_pandemic_in_Peru&action=edit)]

In [Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peru "Peru"), the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") has resulted in 4,533,862[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-Template:COVID-19_data-56) confirmed cases of [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19") and 221,072[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-Template:COVID-19_data-56) deaths. The virus spread to [Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peru "Peru") on 6 March 2020, when a 25-year-old man who had travelled to Spain, France, and the [Czech Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Czech_Republic "Czech Republic") tested positive.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Peru_:0-112) On 15 March 2020, President [Martín Vizcarra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mart%C3%ADn_Vizcarra "Martín Vizcarra") announced a country-wide [lockdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lockdown "Lockdown"), closing borders, restricting [domestic flights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domestic_flight "Domestic flight"), and forbidding nonessential business operations, excluding [health facilities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_facility "Health facility"), [grocery stores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grocery_store "Grocery store"), [pharmacies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pharmacy "Pharmacy"), and [banks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank "Bank"). As of May 2023, Peru has the [highest COVID-19 death rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_death_rates_by_country "COVID-19 pandemic death rates by country") in the world, with over 6,400 deaths per one million citizens.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Peru_cumulative-113)

### Uruguay

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Uruguay")]

This section is an excerpt from [COVID-19 pandemic in Uruguay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Uruguay "COVID-19 pandemic in Uruguay").[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=COVID-19_pandemic_in_Uruguay&action=edit)]

The [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") in Uruguay has resulted in 1,043,295[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-Template:COVID-19_data-56) confirmed cases of [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19") and 7,697[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-Template:COVID-19_data-56) deaths.

The first cases in [Uruguay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uruguay "Uruguay") were reported on 13 March 2020 by the [Ministry of Public Health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Public_Health_(Uruguay) "Ministry of Public Health (Uruguay)").[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-119) The early cases were imported from [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy "Italy") and [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain "Spain"), with some local transmissions.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Uruguay_:0-120) The majority of early cases were traced to a wedding with 500 people in attendance in [Montevideo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montevideo "Montevideo"), attended by a Uruguayan fashion designer who returned from Spain and later tested positive.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Uruguay_Half_of_Uruguay-121)[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-122) Various containment measures were introduced in mid-March, and major restrictions on movement followed in late March. Uruguay is one of the few countries in Latin America to have been able to avoid large outbreaks for a considerable amount of time due to their closing of borders with neighboring countries. The country had one of the lowest numbers of active cases per population in South America up until December when the public health authorities announced that large outbreaks had led to community transmission in Montevideo.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-123) On 23 January 2021, [President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Uruguay "President of Uruguay")[Luis Lacalle Pou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Lacalle_Pou "Luis Lacalle Pou") announced during a press conference that the government purchased doses of [COVID-19 vaccines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_vaccine "COVID-19 vaccine") from [Pfizer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pfizer "Pfizer") and [Sinovac Biotech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinovac_Biotech "Sinovac Biotech"), while negotiating with a third manufacturer.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Uruguay_:1-124)

### Venezuela

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Venezuela")]

Main article: [COVID-19 pandemic in Venezuela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Venezuela "COVID-19 pandemic in Venezuela")

On 13 March, Vice President [Delcy Rodríguez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delcy_Rodr%C3%ADguez "Delcy Rodríguez") announced the first two confirmed cases in the country.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-125)

On 14 March, Communication Minister [Jorge Rodríguez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jorge_Rodr%C3%ADguez_(Venezuelan_politician) "Jorge Rodríguez (Venezuelan politician)") informed that eight new cases were detected in the country.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-126)

On 26 March, the first death was reported.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-Reutersfirstdeath-127)

[Diosdado Cabello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diosdado_Cabello "Diosdado Cabello"), vice-president of the [United Socialist Party of Venezuela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Socialist_Party_of_Venezuela "United Socialist Party of Venezuela") and president of the pro-government [Constituent National Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Constituent_National_Assembly "2017 Constituent National Assembly") announced he tested positive for COVID-19 on 9 July.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-128)

[Tareck El Aissami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tareck_El_Aissami "Tareck El Aissami"), the Minister of Petroleum and [Omar Prieto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omar_Prieto "Omar Prieto"), the [Governor of Zulia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Zulia "Governor of Zulia") also tested positive on 10 July.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-129)

A member of the [2017 National Constituent Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Constituent_National_Assembly "2017 Constituent National Assembly") and the [Governor of the Capital District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Venezuela_governors "List of Venezuela governors"), [Darío Vivas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dar%C3%ADo_Vivas "Darío Vivas") tested positive for COVID-19 on 19 July.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-Vivas-130)

Venezuela Minister of Communication and Information [Jorge Rodríguez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jorge_Rodr%C3%ADguez_(Venezuelan_politician) "Jorge Rodríguez (Venezuelan politician)") tested positive for COVID-19 on 13 August.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-131) On the same day, [Darío Vivas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dar%C3%ADo_Vivas "Darío Vivas") died of COVID-19 at the age of 70.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-Vivas-130)

Venezuela is particularly vulnerable to the wider effects of the [pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") because of its [ongoing socioeconomic and political crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crisis_in_Venezuela "Crisis in Venezuela") causing [massive shortages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shortages_in_Venezuela "Shortages in Venezuela") of food staples and basic necessities, including medical supplies. The [mass emigration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venezuelan_refugee_crisis "Venezuelan refugee crisis") of Venezuelan doctors has also caused chronic staff shortages in hospitals.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-132)

## Prevention in other countries and territories

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Prevention in other countries and territories")]

### South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands")]

[This remote territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Georgia_and_the_South_Sandwich_Islands "South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands") is uninhabited, save for small communities of scientists; the territory is also occasionally visited by small groups of tourists.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-133) On 17 March tourist facilities in [Grytviken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grytviken "Grytviken") were closed as a precaution,[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-134) with various other measures being implemented to protect workers on the islands.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-135) South Georgia is open for visitors with a permit and is still virus free as of 22 April.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-136)

The [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") was confirmed to have reached [South America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_America "South America") on 26 February 2020 when Brazil confirmed a case in [São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Paulo "São Paulo").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-2) By 3 April, all countries and territories in South America had recorded at least one case.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-Stuff/Fairfax-3)

On 13 May 2020, it was reported that Latin America and the [Caribbean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean "Caribbean") had reported over 400,000 cases of COVID-19 infection with, 23,091 deaths. On 22 May 2020, citing the rapid increase of [infections in Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil "COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil"), the [World Health Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Health_Organization "World Health Organization") declared South America the epicentre of the pandemic.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-5)

As of 12 January 2023, South America had recorded 67,331,547 confirmed cases and 1,344,031 deaths from COVID-19. Due to a shortage of testing and medical facilities, it is believed that the outbreak is far larger than the official numbers show.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-6)

### Argentina

[![Image 27](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/75/COVID-19_Pandemic_Cases_in_Argentina_by_number_by_province.svg/250px-COVID-19_Pandemic_Cases_in_Argentina_by_number_by_province.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:COVID-19_Pandemic_Cases_in_Argentina_by_number_by_province.svg)

COVID-19 pandemic cases in Argentina

This section is an excerpt from [COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Argentina "COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina").[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=COVID-19_pandemic_in_Argentina&action=edit)]

The [COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Argentina "COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina") is part of the [worldwide pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") of coronavirus disease 2019 ([COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19")) caused by [severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Severe_acute_respiratory_syndrome_coronavirus_2 "Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2") (SARS-CoV-2). As of 18 September 2026, a total of 10,119,840 people were confirmed to have been infected, and 130,859 people were known to have died because of the virus.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-36)

On 3 March 2020, the virus was confirmed to have spread to [Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentina "Argentina").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-37)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Argentina_InfobaePrimer-38)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-39)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-40) On 7 March 2020, the [Ministry of Health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Health_(Argentina) "Ministry of Health (Argentina)") confirmed the country's first documented death, a 64-year-old man who had travelled to Paris, France, who also had other health conditions; the case was only confirmed as positive after the patient's demise.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Argentina_argentina.1-41)

On 19 March 2020, a nationwide lockdown was established in Argentina.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Argentina_quarantine-42)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Argentina_lockdown-43) The lockdown was lifted throughout all the country, excepting the [Greater Buenos Aires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Buenos_Aires "Greater Buenos Aires") urban area (where 31.9% of the country's population live),[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-44) on 10 May, with Greater Buenos Aires locked down until 17 July, where the lockdown was due to be gradually loosened in several stages to lead to the return to normality;[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Argentina_lockdown-end-17jul-45) restrictions were extended several times until 8 November 2020.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Argentina_lockdown-end-46) During the second wave, another nationwide lockdown took place from 22 to 31 May 2021.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Argentina_lockdown-may-21-47)

Responses to the outbreak have included [restrictions on commerce and movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stay-at-home_order "Stay-at-home order"), closure of borders, and the closure of schools and educational institutions.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Argentina_15Mar-sus-48) Clusters of infections and deaths have occurred in [nursing homes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nursing_home "Nursing home"), prisons and other detention centers, and urban areas.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-49)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-50) The number of tests increased over time, although there were some concerns as there was less testing than in other countries of the region such as Chile and Peru.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Argentina_tests-region-51) Even so, the government's responses to the pandemic were among the best received by the population in the region during the early stages of the pandemic.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Argentina_reception-LatAm-52)

### Bolivia

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Bolivia")]

This section is an excerpt from [COVID-19 pandemic in Bolivia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Bolivia "COVID-19 pandemic in Bolivia").[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=COVID-19_pandemic_in_Bolivia&action=edit)]

The [COVID-19 pandemic in Bolivia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Bolivia "COVID-19 pandemic in Bolivia") was a part of the [worldwide pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") of [coronavirus disease 2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19") (COVID-19) caused by [severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Severe_acute_respiratory_syndrome_coronavirus_2 "Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2") (SARS-CoV-2). The virus was confirmed to have spread to [Bolivia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolivia "Bolivia") on 10 March 2020, when its first two cases were confirmed in the departments of [Oruro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oruro_Department "Oruro Department") and [Santa Cruz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Cruz_Department_(Bolivia) "Santa Cruz Department (Bolivia)").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-53)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-54)

On 12 March, Bolivia suspended all public school sessions until 31 March, as well as all commercial flights to and from Europe indefinitely. They also prohibited large-scale public gatherings of more than 1,000 people.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-55)

### Brazil

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Brazil")]

This section is an excerpt from [COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil "COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil").[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil&action=edit)]

The [COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil "COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil") has resulted in 38,050,567[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-Template:COVID-19_data-56) confirmed cases of [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19") and 704,066[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-Template:COVID-19_data-56) deaths. The virus was confirmed to have spread to [Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil "Brazil") on 25 February 2020,[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-57) when a man from [São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Paulo "São Paulo") who had traveled to [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy "Italy")[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-58) tested positive for the virus. The disease had spread to every [federative unit of Brazil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federative_units_of_Brazil "Federative units of Brazil") by 21 March. On 19 June 2020, the country reported its one millionth case and nearly 49,000 reported deaths.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-59)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-60) One estimate of [under-reporting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Under-reporting#Disease "Under-reporting") was 22.62% of total reported COVID-19 mortality in 2020.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-61)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-62)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-63)

The [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") triggered a variety of responses from federal, state and local governments, having an impact on politics, education, the environment,[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil_AmazonABC-64) and the economy. On 27 March 2020 Brazil announced a temporary ban on foreign air travelers[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-65) and most state governors have imposed quarantines to prevent the spread of the virus.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-66) President [Jair Bolsonaro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jair_Bolsonaro "Jair Bolsonaro") perpetuated [conspiracy theories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_misinformation "COVID-19 misinformation") surrounding COVID-19 treatments[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil_:7-67) and its origins,[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil_:8-68) and was accused of downplaying effective mitigations and pursuing a strategy of [herd immunity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herd_immunity "Herd immunity").[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil_:9-69) In October 2021, a congressional panel recommended criminal charges against the president for his handling of the pandemic, including [crimes against humanity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crimes_against_humanity "Crimes against humanity").[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Brazil_:9-69)

As of 18 September 2026, Brazil, with 38,050,567[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-Template:COVID-19_data-56) confirmed cases and 704,066[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-Template:COVID-19_data-56) deaths, has the third-highest number of confirmed cases and second-highest death toll from COVID-19 in the world, behind only [those of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_the_United_States "COVID-19 pandemic in the United States") and [of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_India "COVID-19 pandemic in India").

### Chile

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Chile")]

This section is an excerpt from [COVID-19 pandemic in Chile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Chile "COVID-19 pandemic in Chile").[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=COVID-19_pandemic_in_Chile&action=edit)]

The [worldwide pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") of coronavirus disease 2019 ([COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19")) caused by [severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SARS-CoV-2 "SARS-CoV-2") (SARS-CoV-2) severely affected [Chile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chile "Chile"). The virus was confirmed to have reached Chile on 3 March 2020.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Chile_First_Case-70) Initial cases had been imported from Southeast Asia and Europe, and expanded into a large number of untraceable infections, placing the country within phase 4 of the pandemic as defined by the [World Health Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Health_Organization "World Health Organization"), with over 1,000 confirmed cases by 25 March 2020.

The cases were concentrated in the [Santiago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santiago "Santiago") metropolitan area, with outbreaks in other regions in the country. No national [lockdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lockdown "Lockdown") was established in Chile, unlike [in neighboring Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Argentina "COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina") and [Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Peru "COVID-19 pandemic in Peru"), although a night [curfew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curfew "Curfew") was implemented throughout the country. Quarantines were established locally in different cities and neighborhoods. However, in May 2020 the whole city of Santiago was put under mandatory quarantine due to an increase of cases, and similar situations were extended to most of the largest cities in Chile.

Considering its population, by June 2020 Chile had one of the worst outbreaks in the world.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-71) Initially, the number of fatalities reported was lower than in other countries in South America, even those with fewer cases. However, in May 2020, the number of cases and deaths increased rapidly, while several sources reported [excess deaths](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mortality_displacement "Mortality displacement") not officially attributed to COVID-19, which were not counted.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Chile_excess_deaths_nyt-72)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-73) By June 2020, the government confirmed thousands of additional deaths due to COVID-19, including suspected cases where [PCR tests](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_testing "COVID-19 testing") were not available.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Chile_sospechosos-74) The pandemic reached a peak on 13 June with 195 daily confirmed deaths and nearly 7,000 positive cases.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Chile_Govt_Report-75) By July 2020, 10,000 people had died, and Chile had the sixth largest number of cases in the world.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Chile_epidem5jul-76)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-77) In the following weeks, the number of daily cases and deaths started to decrease slowly, although some local outbreaks appeared. The number of cases increased later in the year, and by March 2021 the number of daily cases had exceeded those in the initial wave.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Chile_:1-78)

Chile became one of the first countries to start a nationwide program to [vaccinate against COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_vaccine "COVID-19 vaccine"). On 24 December 2020, the first batch of vaccines arrived in the country to inoculate mainly health workers.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Chile_:2-79) With larger batches of vaccines (mainly [Sinovac's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinovac_Biotech "Sinovac Biotech")[CoronaVac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CoronaVac "CoronaVac")) arriving from February 2021, Chile became one of the fastest countries in the world to inoculate their population: by March 2021 a quarter of the population had received at least one dose. This fast response was due to signing contracts with multiple providers, a strong public immunization program, and little [anti-vaccine sentiment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-vaccine_sentiment "Anti-vaccine sentiment").[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-80) Despite the success of the vaccination program the number of cases increased, which has been attributed to early relaxation of restrictions and a false sense of security.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-81)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-82)[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-83)

With more than 92,000 cases and 2,500 deaths per million inhabitants,[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Chile_Govt_Report-75) the [impact of the pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_of_the_COVID-19_pandemic "Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic") has been great in the South American country. In March 2020, when the first cases of COVID-19 were reported, the country was still facing [protests and riots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%932022_Chilean_protests "2019–2022 Chilean protests")[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-eyes-85) that had begun in October 2019, and the pandemic affected the scheduled [2020 Chilean constitutional referendum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Chilean_constitutional_referendum "2020 Chilean constitutional referendum"), which was rescheduled and held later in the year. Partial lockdowns and quarantines were established in the first months, [hitting the economy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economic_impact_of_the_COVID-19_pandemic "Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic") of the country. By April 2020, unemployment had reached 9%, a ten-year high.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-86)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-87) A wave of protests sparked in late May, mainly in Santiago, due to food shortages in certain sectors of the population.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-88) The Chilean GDP shrank by a 5.8% in 2020, the largest recession in 40 years in the country.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-89) Chile is the only country in the world with entry procedures such as requiring homologation of vaccines to travel to.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-90)

### Colombia

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Colombia")]

This section is an excerpt from [COVID-19 pandemic in Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Colombia "COVID-19 pandemic in Colombia").[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=COVID-19_pandemic_in_Colombia&action=edit)]

The [COVID-19 pandemic in Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Colombia "COVID-19 pandemic in Colombia") was a part of the [pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") of [coronavirus disease 2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19") (COVID-19) caused by [severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Severe_acute_respiratory_syndrome_coronavirus_2 "Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2") (SARS-CoV-2). The virus was confirmed to have reached [Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia "Colombia") on 6 March 2020.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Colombia_reuters6march-91)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-92)

Up to January 2022, four waves affected Colombia: Infections and deaths peaked in August 2020, again in January 2021 following the Christmas holidays, reached new highs between April and June 2021, and a fourth wave was confirmed in late December 2021 following the arrival of the [Omicron variant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SARS-CoV-2_Omicron_variant "SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant") of SARS-CoV-2.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-93)

"Confirmed COVID-19" was the primary cause of death in Colombia in 2020, where the virus caused over 50,000 fatalities by the end of the calendar year. An additional 13,000 deaths in Colombia that year were suspected to be caused by COVID-19, making "suspected COVID-19" the third most common cause of death.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-94) The "confirmed COVID-19" death toll doubled during the first half of 2021, reaching 100,000 before the end of June (including all deaths from the beginning of the pandemic).[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-95)

### Ecuador

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Ecuador")]

Main article: [COVID-19 pandemic in Ecuador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Ecuador "COVID-19 pandemic in Ecuador")

[![Image 28](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0a/COVID-19_Outbreak_Cases_in_Ecuador.svg/250px-COVID-19_Outbreak_Cases_in_Ecuador.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:COVID-19_Outbreak_Cases_in_Ecuador.svg)

Confirmed COVID-19 cases in Ecuador

On 29 February 2020, the [Minister of Health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_minister "Health minister") in Ecuador, Catalina Andramuño, confirmed the first case of the virus in the country.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-ecuador.1-96) The person, an elderly woman, was an Ecuadorian citizen residing in Spain who had arrived to Guayaquil on 14 February without showing symptoms. She fell ill and was hospitalized, where she was diagnosed with COVID.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-ecuador.1-96)

On 1 March 2020, Andramuño announced that five new cases of coronavirus have been confirmed in Ecuador.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-97)

As of 31 March 2020, there have been 2240 confirmed cases, plus 75 deaths linked to COVID-19. The Health Ministry also reported 61 deaths probably related to COVID-19.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-98)

Ecuador was described in April 2020 as emerging as the "epicentre" of the pandemic in Latin America.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-Stuff/Fairfax-3) The [Guayas Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guayas_Province "Guayas Province") was particularly strongly affected, with thousand of excess deaths reported compared to the figure for a normal period.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-bbc_ecuador-99) It was reported on 17 April 2020 that 10,939 people had died in six weeks since the start of March in the [Guayas Province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guayas_Province "Guayas Province"), compared to a normal figure of 3,000 for the province.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-collyns-100)

### Peru

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Peru")]

This section is an excerpt from [COVID-19 pandemic in Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Peru "COVID-19 pandemic in Peru").[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=COVID-19_pandemic_in_Peru&action=edit)]

In [Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peru "Peru"), the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") has resulted in 4,533,862[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-Template:COVID-19_data-56) confirmed cases of [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19") and 221,072[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-Template:COVID-19_data-56) deaths. The virus spread to [Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peru "Peru") on 6 March 2020, when a 25-year-old man who had travelled to Spain, France, and the [Czech Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Czech_Republic "Czech Republic") tested positive.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Peru_:0-112) On 15 March 2020, President [Martín Vizcarra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mart%C3%ADn_Vizcarra "Martín Vizcarra") announced a country-wide [lockdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lockdown "Lockdown"), closing borders, restricting [domestic flights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domestic_flight "Domestic flight"), and forbidding nonessential business operations, excluding [health facilities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_facility "Health facility"), [grocery stores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grocery_store "Grocery store"), [pharmacies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pharmacy "Pharmacy"), and [banks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank "Bank"). As of May 2023, Peru has the [highest COVID-19 death rate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_death_rates_by_country "COVID-19 pandemic death rates by country") in the world, with over 6,400 deaths per one million citizens.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Peru_cumulative-113)

### Uruguay

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Uruguay")]

This section is an excerpt from [COVID-19 pandemic in Uruguay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Uruguay "COVID-19 pandemic in Uruguay").[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=COVID-19_pandemic_in_Uruguay&action=edit)]

The [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") in Uruguay has resulted in 1,043,295[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-Template:COVID-19_data-56) confirmed cases of [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19 "COVID-19") and 7,697[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-Template:COVID-19_data-56) deaths.

The first cases in [Uruguay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uruguay "Uruguay") were reported on 13 March 2020 by the [Ministry of Public Health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ministry_of_Public_Health_(Uruguay) "Ministry of Public Health (Uruguay)").[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-119) The early cases were imported from [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy "Italy") and [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain "Spain"), with some local transmissions.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Uruguay_:0-120) The majority of early cases were traced to a wedding with 500 people in attendance in [Montevideo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montevideo "Montevideo"), attended by a Uruguayan fashion designer who returned from Spain and later tested positive.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Uruguay_Half_of_Uruguay-121)[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-122) Various containment measures were introduced in mid-March, and major restrictions on movement followed in late March. Uruguay is one of the few countries in Latin America to have been able to avoid large outbreaks for a considerable amount of time due to their closing of borders with neighboring countries. The country had one of the lowest numbers of active cases per population in South America up until December when the public health authorities announced that large outbreaks had led to community transmission in Montevideo.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-123) On 23 January 2021, [President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Uruguay "President of Uruguay")[Luis Lacalle Pou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Lacalle_Pou "Luis Lacalle Pou") announced during a press conference that the government purchased doses of [COVID-19 vaccines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_vaccine "COVID-19 vaccine") from [Pfizer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pfizer "Pfizer") and [Sinovac Biotech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinovac_Biotech "Sinovac Biotech"), while negotiating with a third manufacturer.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-COVID-19_pandemic_in_Uruguay_:1-124)

### Venezuela

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Venezuela")]

Main article: [COVID-19 pandemic in Venezuela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Venezuela "COVID-19 pandemic in Venezuela")

On 13 March, Vice President [Delcy Rodríguez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delcy_Rodr%C3%ADguez "Delcy Rodríguez") announced the first two confirmed cases in the country.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-125)

On 14 March, Communication Minister [Jorge Rodríguez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jorge_Rodr%C3%ADguez_(Venezuelan_politician) "Jorge Rodríguez (Venezuelan politician)") informed that eight new cases were detected in the country.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-126)

On 26 March, the first death was reported.[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-Reutersfirstdeath-127)

[Diosdado Cabello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diosdado_Cabello "Diosdado Cabello"), vice-president of the [United Socialist Party of Venezuela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Socialist_Party_of_Venezuela "United Socialist Party of Venezuela") and president of the pro-government [Constituent National Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Constituent_National_Assembly "2017 Constituent National Assembly") announced he tested positive for COVID-19 on 9 July.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-128)

[Tareck El Aissami](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tareck_El_Aissami "Tareck El Aissami"), the Minister of Petroleum and [Omar Prieto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omar_Prieto "Omar Prieto"), the [Governor of Zulia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_Zulia "Governor of Zulia") also tested positive on 10 July.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-129)

A member of the [2017 National Constituent Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Constituent_National_Assembly "2017 Constituent National Assembly") and the [Governor of the Capital District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Venezuela_governors "List of Venezuela governors"), [Darío Vivas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dar%C3%ADo_Vivas "Darío Vivas") tested positive for COVID-19 on 19 July.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-Vivas-130)

Venezuela Minister of Communication and Information [Jorge Rodríguez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jorge_Rodr%C3%ADguez_(Venezuelan_politician) "Jorge Rodríguez (Venezuelan politician)") tested positive for COVID-19 on 13 August.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-131) On the same day, [Darío Vivas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dar%C3%ADo_Vivas "Darío Vivas") died of COVID-19 at the age of 70.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-Vivas-130)

Venezuela is particularly vulnerable to the wider effects of the [pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic") because of its [ongoing socioeconomic and political crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crisis_in_Venezuela "Crisis in Venezuela") causing [massive shortages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shortages_in_Venezuela "Shortages in Venezuela") of food staples and basic necessities, including medical supplies. The [mass emigration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venezuelan_refugee_crisis "Venezuelan refugee crisis") of Venezuelan doctors has also caused chronic staff shortages in hospitals.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-132)

### South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands")]

[This remote territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Georgia_and_the_South_Sandwich_Islands "South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands") is uninhabited, save for small communities of scientists; the territory is also occasionally visited by small groups of tourists.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-133) On 17 March tourist facilities in [Grytviken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grytviken "Grytviken") were closed as a precaution,[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-134) with various other measures being implemented to protect workers on the islands.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-135) South Georgia is open for visitors with a permit and is still virus free as of 22 April.[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_South_America#cite_note-136)
