The **United Nations** (**UN**) is an international [intergovernmental organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intergovernmental_organization "Intergovernmental organization") established by the signing of the [Charter of the United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charter_of_the_United_Nations "Charter of the United Nations") on 26 June 1945 with the articulated mission of maintaining [international peace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_peace "International peace") and [security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_security "International security"), to develop friendly [relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diplomacy "Diplomacy") among [states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_(polity) "State (polity)"), to promote international cooperation, and to serve as a centre for harmonizing the actions of states in achieving those goals.

The [United Nations headquarters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_headquarters "United Nations headquarters") is located in New York City, with several other offices located in [Geneva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Office_at_Geneva "United Nations Office at Geneva"), [Nairobi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Office_at_Nairobi "United Nations Office at Nairobi"), [Vienna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Office_at_Vienna "United Nations Office at Vienna") and [The Hague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hague "The Hague"). The UN comprises six principal organizations: [General Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_General_Assembly "United Nations General Assembly"), [Security Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council "United Nations Security Council"), [Economic and Social Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Economic_and_Social_Council "United Nations Economic and Social Council"), [International Court of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Court_of_Justice "International Court of Justice"), [Secretariat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Secretariat "United Nations Secretariat") and [Trusteeship Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Trusteeship_Council "United Nations Trusteeship Council") which, together with several [specialized agencies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_specialized_agencies_of_the_United_Nations "List of specialized agencies of the United Nations") and related agencies, make up the [UN System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_System "United Nations System"). There is a total of 193 [member states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_states_of_the_United_Nations "Member states of the United Nations"), representing nearly all of the world's [sovereign states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sovereign_state "Sovereign state"), as well as two [observer states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_General_Assembly_observers "United Nations General Assembly observers"), the [Holy See](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_See "Holy See") and the [State of Palestine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestine "Palestine").

The United Nations has primarily focused on economic and social development, particularly during the wave of [decolonization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decolonization "Decolonization") in the mid-twentieth century. The UN currently operates [11 peacekeeping missions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_peacekeeping "United Nations peacekeeping"), by order of inception, in [the Middle East](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Truce_Supervision_Organization "United Nations Truce Supervision Organization"), [Kashmir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UN_mediation_of_the_Kashmir_dispute "UN mediation of the Kashmir dispute"), [Cyprus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Peacekeeping_Force_in_Cyprus "United Nations Peacekeeping Force in Cyprus"), the [Golan Heights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Disengagement_Observer_Force "United Nations Disengagement Observer Force"), [Lebanon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Interim_Force_in_Lebanon "United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon"), the [Western Sahara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Mission_for_the_Referendum_in_Western_Sahara "United Nations Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara"), [Kosovo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Interim_Administration_Mission_in_Kosovo "United Nations Interim Administration Mission in Kosovo"), the [Democratic Republic of the Congo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MONUSCO "MONUSCO"), [Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Interim_Security_Force_for_Abyei "United Nations Interim Security Force for Abyei"), [South Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Mission_in_South_Sudan "United Nations Mission in South Sudan") and the [Central African Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MINUSCA "MINUSCA"). The UN has been recognized as a global leader of peace and human development, with many officials and agencies having been awarded the [Nobel Peace Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Peace_Prize "Nobel Peace Prize") but has also been [criticized for perceived ineffectiveness, bias, and corruption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Criticism_of_the_United_Nations "Criticism of the United Nations").

## History

Main article: [History of the United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_United_Nations "History of the United Nations")

### Background (pre-1941)

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/16/Emperor_Haile_Selassie_League_of_Nations_speech.png/250px-Emperor_Haile_Selassie_League_of_Nations_speech.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Emperor_Haile_Selassie_League_of_Nations_speech.png)

[Haile Selassie I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Selassie "Haile Selassie") at the [League of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Nations "League of Nations") appealing Italy's 1936 invasion in which the League failed to intervene.

In the century prior to the UN's creation, several [international organizations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_organization "International organization") such as the [International Committee of the Red Cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Committee_of_the_Red_Cross "International Committee of the Red Cross") (ICRC) were formed to ensure protection and assistance for victims of armed conflict and strife.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-5)

During [World War I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I "World War I"), several major leaders, especially then-U.S. President [Woodrow Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodrow_Wilson "Woodrow Wilson"), advocated for a world body to guarantee peace. The winners of the war, the [Allied Powers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allies_of_World_War_I "Allies of World War I"), met to decide on formal peace terms at the [Paris Peace Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Peace_Conference_(1919%E2%80%931920) "Paris Peace Conference (1919–1920)"). The [League of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Nations "League of Nations") was approved and started operations, but the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") never joined. On 10 January 1920, the League of Nations formally came into being when the [Covenant of the League of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Covenant_of_the_League_of_Nations "Covenant of the League of Nations"), ratified by 42 nations in 1919, took effect.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-6) The League of Nations Council acted as an executive body directing the Assembly's business, though with few powers explicitly vested in either body, the League's operation was mostly derived from informal convention than the Covenant itself. With few exceptions, all of the League's substantive decisions required unanimity, a provision negotiated in the name of [upholding national sovereignty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westphalian_sovereignty "Westphalian sovereignty"). It began with four permanent members of the Council—the [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_of_Great_Britain_and_Ireland "United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland"), [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_French_Republic "Third French Republic"), [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Italy "Kingdom of Italy") and [Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_of_Japan "Empire of Japan"). The fifth permanent seat on the Council, meant to be held by the United States, was later given to [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weimar_Republic "Weimar Republic") and, after [its withdrawal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1933_German_League_of_Nations_withdrawal_referendum "1933 German League of Nations withdrawal referendum"), the [Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union"). Forty nations voted for Japan to end [its occupation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_occupation_of_Manchuria "Japanese occupation of Manchuria") of [Manchuria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchuria "Manchuria") but Japan voted against it and withdrew from the League instead.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-7) It also failed to act against the [Second Italo-Ethiopian War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Italo-Ethiopian_War "Second Italo-Ethiopian War"), after the appeal for international intervention by [Ethiopian Emperor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopian_Emperor "Ethiopian Emperor")[Haile Selassie I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Selassie "Haile Selassie") at Geneva in 1936 went with no avail, including when calls for economic sanctions against Italy failed. Italy and other nations left the League.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-8)

When [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") broke out in 1939, the League effectively closed down. Among its final acts was the expulsion of the Soviet Union for the [invasion of Finland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winter_War "Winter War").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-9)

### Declarations by the Allies of World War II (1941–1944)

The first step towards the establishment of the United Nations was the Inter-Allied Conference in London that led to the [Declaration of St James's Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Declaration_of_St_James's_Palace "Declaration of St James's Palace") on 12 June 1941.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-10)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-11) By August 1941, American president [Franklin D. Roosevelt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin_D._Roosevelt "Franklin D. Roosevelt") and British prime minister [Winston Churchill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill "Winston Churchill") had drafted the [Atlantic Charter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Charter "Atlantic Charter"); which defined goals for the post-war world. At the subsequent meeting of the Inter-Allied Council in London on 24 September 1941, the eight [governments in exile of countries under Axis occupation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governments_in_exile_during_World_War_II "List of governments in exile during World War II"), together with the [Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union") and representatives of the [Free French Forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_French_Forces "Free French Forces"), unanimously adopted adherence to the common principles of policy set forth by Britain and the United States.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-12)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-13)

Roosevelt and Churchill met at the [White House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House "White House") in December 1941 for the [Arcadia Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcadia_Conference "Arcadia Conference"). Roosevelt is considered a founder of the UN,[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-14)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-15) and coined the term _United Nations_ to describe the [Allied countries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allies_of_World_War_II "Allies of World War II").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-16) Churchill accepted it, noting its use by [Lord Byron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lord_Byron "Lord Byron").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-17) The text of the [Declaration by United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Declaration_by_United_Nations "Declaration by United Nations") was drafted on 29 December 1941, by Roosevelt, Churchill, and [Harry Hopkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Hopkins "Harry Hopkins"). It incorporated Soviet suggestions but included no role for France. One major change from the Atlantic Charter was the addition of a provision for [religious freedom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Religious_freedom "Religious freedom"), which Stalin approved after Roosevelt insisted.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-18)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-FOOTNOTESherwood1948447%E2%80%93453-19)

Roosevelt's idea of the "[Four Powers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Four_Policemen "Four Policemen")" refers to the four major Allied countries, the United States, the United Kingdom, the Soviet Union, and [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_China_(1912%E2%80%931949) "Republic of China (1912–1949)"), emerged in the Declaration by the United Nations.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-sheriff-20) On New Year's Day 1942, Roosevelt, Churchill, the Soviet Union's former Foreign Minister [Maxim Litvinov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxim_Litvinov "Maxim Litvinov"), and the Chinese Premier [T. V. Soong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._V._Soong "T. V. Soong") signed the "[Declaration by United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Declaration_by_United_Nations "Declaration by United Nations")",[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-21) and the next day the representatives of twenty-two other nations added their signatures. During the war, the United Nations became the official term for the Allies. In order to join, countries had to sign the Declaration and declare war on the [Axis powers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axis_powers "Axis powers").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-FOOTNOTESchlesinger2003-22)

The October 1943 [Moscow Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow_Conference_(1943) "Moscow Conference (1943)") resulted in the [Moscow Declarations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow_Declarations "Moscow Declarations"), including the [Four Power Declaration on General Security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Four_Nations "Declaration of the Four Nations"). This declaration was signed by the [Allied Big Four](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Four_(World_War_II) "Big Four (World War II)")—the United States, the Soviet Union, the United Kingdom, and China—and aimed for the creation "at the earliest possible date of a general international organization". This was the first public announcement that a new international organization was being contemplated to replace the League of Nations. The [Tehran Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tehran_Conference "Tehran Conference") followed shortly afterwards at which Roosevelt, Churchill and [Joseph Stalin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Stalin "Joseph Stalin"), the leader of the Soviet Union, met and discussed the idea of a post-war international organization.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-23)

The new international organization was formulated and negotiated amongst the delegations from the [Allied Big Four](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Four_(World_War_II) "Big Four (World War II)") at the [Dumbarton Oaks Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dumbarton_Oaks_Conference "Dumbarton Oaks Conference") from 21 September to 7 October 1944. They agreed on proposals for the aims, structure and functioning of the new organization.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-Bohlen_1973-24)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-25)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-26) It took the [conference at Yalta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yalta_Conference "Yalta Conference") in February 1945, and further negotiations with the Soviet Union, before all the issues were resolved.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-Bohlen_1973-24)

### Founding (1945)

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3a/United_Nations_Member_States-1945.png/500px-United_Nations_Member_States-1945.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:United_Nations_Member_States-1945.png)

The UN in 1945: founding members in light blue, protectorates and territories of the founding members in dark blue (Some nations' land would be different from now.)

By 1 March 1945, 21 additional states had signed the Declaration by the United Nations.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-FOOTNOTEOsma%C5%84czyk20042445-27) After months of planning, the [UN Conference on International Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Conference_on_International_Organization "United Nations Conference on International Organization") opened in [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco") on 25 April 1945. It was attended by 50 nations' governments and a number of non-governmental organizations.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-Charter-28)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-UNHistory-29)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-30) The delegations of the Big Four chaired the plenary meetings.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-31) Previously, Churchill had urged Roosevelt to restore France to its status of a major power after the [liberation of Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberation_of_Paris "Liberation of Paris") in August 1944. The drafting of the [Charter of the United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charter_of_the_United_Nations "Charter of the United Nations") was completed over the following two months, and it was signed on 26 June 1945 by the representatives of the 50 countries.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-32)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-33) The UN officially came into existence at 20:07 ([UTC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coordinated_Universal_Time "Coordinated Universal Time")) on 24 October 1945,[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-34)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-35) upon ratification of the Charter by the five permanent members of the [Security Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council "United Nations Security Council"): the United States, the United Kingdom, France, the Soviet Union and [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_China_(1912%E2%80%931949) "Republic of China (1912–1949)") — and by a majority of the other 46 nations.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-unmilestones1941to1950-36)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-original_draft-37)

The [first meetings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_session_of_the_United_Nations_General_Assembly "First session of the United Nations General Assembly") of the [General Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Assembly "General Assembly"), with 51 nations represented,[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-40) and the Security Council took place in London beginning in January 1946.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-unmilestones1941to1950-36) Debates began at once, covering topical issues such as the presence of Soviet troops in [Iranian Azerbaijan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iranian_Azerbaijan "Iranian Azerbaijan") and British forces in [Greece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greece "Greece").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-41) British diplomat [Gladwyn Jebb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gladwyn_Jebb "Gladwyn Jebb") served as interim secretary-general.

The General Assembly selected New York City as the site for the headquarters of the UN. Construction began on 14 September 1948 and the facility was completed on 9 October 1952. The Norwegian Foreign Minister, [Trygve Lie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trygve_Lie "Trygve Lie"), was the first elected [UN secretary-general](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary-General_of_the_United_Nations "Secretary-General of the United Nations").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-unmilestones1941to1950-36)

### Cold War (1947–1991)

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f1/Dag_Hammarskj%C3%B6ld_%283x4_cropped%29.jpg/250px-Dag_Hammarskj%C3%B6ld_%283x4_cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dag_Hammarskj%C3%B6ld_(3x4_cropped).jpg)

[Dag Hammarskjöld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dag_Hammarskj%C3%B6ld "Dag Hammarskjöld") was a particularly active secretary-general from 1953 until his death in 1961.

Though the UN's primary mandate was [peacekeeping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peacekeeping "Peacekeeping"), the division between the United States and the Soviet Union often paralysed the organization; this generally allowed it to intervene only in conflicts distant from the [Cold War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War "Cold War").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMeisler199535-42) Two notable exceptions were a Security Council resolution on 7 July 1950 authorizing a [US-led coalition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Command "United Nations Command") to repel the [North Korean invasion of South Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Pokpung "Operation Pokpung"), passed in the absence of the Soviet Union,[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-unmilestones1941to1950-36)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMeisler199558%E2%80%9359-43) and the signing of the [Korean Armistice Agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_Armistice_Agreement "Korean Armistice Agreement") on 27 July 1953.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-44)

On 29 November 1947, the General Assembly approved [Resolution 181](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Partition_Plan_for_Palestine "United Nations Partition Plan for Palestine"), a proposal to partition British Mandatory [Palestine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandatory_Palestine "Mandatory Palestine") into two states, a Jewish state and an Arab state, with Jerusalem placed under international status.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-45) The Partition plan passed 33–13 with 10 abstentions and one absent. The plan was accepted by the Jews and rejected by the Arabs of Palestine and the Arab states [[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-186-20240719-46) leading to [civil war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1947%E2%80%931948_civil_war_in_Mandatory_Palestine "1947–1948 civil war in Mandatory Palestine"). Following the declaration of the State of Israel on 15 May 1948, the surrounding Arab armies invaded Palestine,[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-47) beginning the [1948 Arab–Israeli War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_Arab%E2%80%93Israeli_War "1948 Arab–Israeli War").[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-48) Two years later, [Ralph Bunche](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_Bunche "Ralph Bunche"), a UN official, negotiated [an armistice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1949_Armistice_Agreements "1949 Armistice Agreements") to the [resulting conflict](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1948_Palestine_war "1948 Palestine war"), with the Security Council deciding that "an armistice shall be established in all sectors of Palestine."[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-186-20240719-46)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMeisler199551%E2%80%9354-49) On 7 November 1956, the [first UN peacekeeping force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Emergency_Force "United Nations Emergency Force") was established to end the [Suez Crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suez_Crisis "Suez Crisis");[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-unmilestones1951to1960-50) however, the UN was unable to intervene against the Soviet Union's simultaneous invasion of [Hungary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungary "Hungary"), following [the country's revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_Revolution_of_1956 "Hungarian Revolution of 1956").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMeisler1995114-51)

On 14 July 1960, the UN established the [United Nations Operation in the Congo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Operation_in_the_Congo "United Nations Operation in the Congo") (UNOC), the largest military force of its early decades, to bring order to [Katanga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_of_Katanga "State of Katanga"), restoring it to the control of the [Democratic Republic of the Congo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_the_Congo_(L%C3%A9opoldville) "Republic of the Congo (Léopoldville)") by 11 May 1964.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMeisler1995115%E2%80%93134-52) While travelling to meet rebel leader [Moise Tshombe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moise_Tshombe "Moise Tshombe") during the conflict, [Dag Hammarskjöld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dag_Hammarskj%C3%B6ld "Dag Hammarskjöld"), often named as one of the UN's most effective secretaries-general,[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMeisler199576-53)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKennedy200760-54)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFasulo200417,_20-55)[died in a plane crash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1961_Ndola_United_Nations_DC-6_crash "1961 Ndola United Nations DC-6 crash"). The **United Nations** (**UN**) is an international [intergovernmental organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intergovernmental_organization "Intergovernmental organization") established by the signing of the [Charter of the United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charter_of_the_United_Nations "Charter of the United Nations") on 26 June 1945 with the articulated mission of maintaining [international peace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_peace "International peace") and [security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_security "International security"), to develop friendly [relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diplomacy "Diplomacy") among [states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_(polity) "State (polity)"), to promote international cooperation, and to serve as a centre for harmonizing the actions of states in achieving those goals.

The [United Nations headquarters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_headquarters "United Nations headquarters") is located in New York City, with several other offices located in [Geneva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Office_at_Geneva "United Nations Office at Geneva"), [Nairobi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Office_at_Nairobi "United Nations Office at Nairobi"), [Vienna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Office_at_Vienna "United Nations Office at Vienna") and [The Hague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Hague "The Hague"). The UN comprises six principal organizations: [General Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_General_Assembly "United Nations General Assembly"), [Security Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council "United Nations Security Council"), [Economic and Social Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Economic_and_Social_Council "United Nations Economic and Social Council"), [International Court of Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Court_of_Justice "International Court of Justice"), [Secretariat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Secretariat "United Nations Secretariat") and [Trusteeship Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Trusteeship_Council "United Nations Trusteeship Council") which, together with several [specialized agencies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_specialized_agencies_of_the_United_Nations "List of specialized agencies of the United Nations") and related agencies, make up the [UN System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_System "United Nations System"). There is a total of 193 [member states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_states_of_the_United_Nations "Member states of the United Nations"), representing nearly all of the world's [sovereign states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sovereign_state "Sovereign state"), as well as two [observer states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_General_Assembly_observers "United Nations General Assembly observers"), the [Holy See](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_See "Holy See") and the [State of Palestine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestine "Palestine").

The United Nations has primarily focused on economic and social development, particularly during the wave of [decolonization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decolonization "Decolonization") in the mid-twentieth century. The UN currently operates [11 peacekeeping missions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_peacekeeping "United Nations peacekeeping"), by order of inception, in [the Middle East](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Truce_Supervision_Organization "United Nations Truce Supervision Organization"), [Kashmir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UN_mediation_of_the_Kashmir_dispute "UN mediation of the Kashmir dispute"), [Cyprus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Peacekeeping_Force_in_Cyprus "United Nations Peacekeeping Force in Cyprus"), the [Golan Heights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Disengagement_Observer_Force "United Nations Disengagement Observer Force"), [Lebanon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Interim_Force_in_Lebanon "United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon"), the [Western Sahara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Mission_for_the_Referendum_in_Western_Sahara "United Nations Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara"), [Kosovo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Interim_Administration_Mission_in_Kosovo "United Nations Interim Administration Mission in Kosovo"), the [Democratic Republic of the Congo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MONUSCO "MONUSCO"), [Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Interim_Security_Force_for_Abyei "United Nations Interim Security Force for Abyei"), [South Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Mission_in_South_Sudan "United Nations Mission in South Sudan") and the [Central African Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MINUSCA "MINUSCA"). The UN has been recognized as a global leader of peace and human development, with many officials and agencies having been awarded the [Nobel Peace Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobel_Peace_Prize "Nobel Peace Prize") but has also been [criticized for perceived ineffectiveness, bias, and corruption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Criticism_of_the_United_Nations "Criticism of the United Nations").

## History

Main article: [History of the United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_United_Nations "History of the United Nations")

### Background (pre-1941)

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/16/Emperor_Haile_Selassie_League_of_Nations_speech.png/250px-Emperor_Haile_Selassie_League_of_Nations_speech.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Emperor_Haile_Selassie_League_of_Nations_speech.png)

[Haile Selassie I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Selassie "Haile Selassie") at the [League of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Nations "League of Nations") appealing Italy's 1936 invasion in which the League failed to intervene.

In the century prior to the UN's creation, several [international organizations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_organization "International organization") such as the [International Committee of the Red Cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Committee_of_the_Red_Cross "International Committee of the Red Cross") (ICRC) were formed to ensure protection and assistance for victims of armed conflict and strife.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-5)

During [World War I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_I "World War I"), several major leaders, especially then-U.S. President [Woodrow Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodrow_Wilson "Woodrow Wilson"), advocated for a world body to guarantee peace. The winners of the war, the [Allied Powers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allies_of_World_War_I "Allies of World War I"), met to decide on formal peace terms at the [Paris Peace Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Peace_Conference_(1919%E2%80%931920) "Paris Peace Conference (1919–1920)"). The [League of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Nations "League of Nations") was approved and started operations, but the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") never joined. On 10 January 1920, the League of Nations formally came into being when the [Covenant of the League of Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Covenant_of_the_League_of_Nations "Covenant of the League of Nations"), ratified by 42 nations in 1919, took effect.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-6) The League of Nations Council acted as an executive body directing the Assembly's business, though with few powers explicitly vested in either body, the League's operation was mostly derived from informal convention than the Covenant itself. With few exceptions, all of the League's substantive decisions required unanimity, a provision negotiated in the name of [upholding national sovereignty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westphalian_sovereignty "Westphalian sovereignty"). It began with four permanent members of the Council—the [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom_of_Great_Britain_and_Ireland "United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland"), [France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_French_Republic "Third French Republic"), [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Italy "Kingdom of Italy") and [Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Empire_of_Japan "Empire of Japan"). The fifth permanent seat on the Council, meant to be held by the United States, was later given to [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weimar_Republic "Weimar Republic") and, after [its withdrawal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1933_German_League_of_Nations_withdrawal_referendum "1933 German League of Nations withdrawal referendum"), the [Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union"). Forty nations voted for Japan to end [its occupation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_occupation_of_Manchuria "Japanese occupation of Manchuria") of [Manchuria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchuria "Manchuria") but Japan voted against it and withdrew from the League instead.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-7) It also failed to act against the [Second Italo-Ethiopian War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Italo-Ethiopian_War "Second Italo-Ethiopian War"), after the appeal for international intervention by [Ethiopian Emperor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopian_Emperor "Ethiopian Emperor")[Haile Selassie I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haile_Selassie "Haile Selassie") at Geneva in 1936 went with no avail, including when calls for economic sanctions against Italy failed. Italy and other nations left the League.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-8)

When [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") broke out in 1939, the League effectively closed down. Among its final acts was the expulsion of the Soviet Union for the [invasion of Finland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winter_War "Winter War").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-9)

### Declarations by the Allies of World War II (1941–1944)

The first step towards the establishment of the United Nations was the Inter-Allied Conference in London that led to the [Declaration of St James's Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Declaration_of_St_James's_Palace "Declaration of St James's Palace") on 12 June 1941.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-10)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-11) By August 1941, American president [Franklin D. Roosevelt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin_D._Roosevelt "Franklin D. Roosevelt") and British prime minister [Winston Churchill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill "Winston Churchill") had drafted the [Atlantic Charter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Charter "Atlantic Charter"); which defined goals for the post-war world. At the subsequent meeting of the Inter-Allied Council in London on 24 September 1941, the eight [governments in exile of countries under Axis occupation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_governments_in_exile_during_World_War_II "List of governments in exile during World War II"), together with the [Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union") and representatives of the [Free French Forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_French_Forces "Free French Forces"), unanimously adopted adherence to the common principles of policy set forth by Britain and the United States.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-12)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-13)

Roosevelt and Churchill met at the [White House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House "White House") in December 1941 for the [Arcadia Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcadia_Conference "Arcadia Conference"). Roosevelt is considered a founder of the UN,[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-14)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-15) and coined the term _United Nations_ to describe the [Allied countries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allies_of_World_War_II "Allies of World War II").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-16) Churchill accepted it, noting its use by [Lord Byron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lord_Byron "Lord Byron").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-17) The text of the [Declaration by United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Declaration_by_United_Nations "Declaration by United Nations") was drafted on 29 December 1941, by Roosevelt, Churchill, and [Harry Hopkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Hopkins "Harry Hopkins"). It incorporated Soviet suggestions but included no role for France. One major change from the Atlantic Charter was the addition of a provision for [religious freedom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Religious_freedom "Religious freedom"), which Stalin approved after Roosevelt insisted.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-18)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-FOOTNOTESherwood1948447%E2%80%93453-19)

Roosevelt's idea of the "[Four Powers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Four_Policemen "Four Policemen")" refers to the four major Allied countries, the United States, the United Kingdom, the Soviet Union, and [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_China_(1912%E2%80%931949) "Republic of China (1912–1949)"), emerged in the Declaration by the United Nations.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-sheriff-20) On New Year's Day 1942, Roosevelt, Churchill, the Soviet Union's former Foreign Minister [Maxim Litvinov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxim_Litvinov "Maxim Litvinov"), and the Chinese Premier [T. V. Soong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T._V._Soong "T. V. Soong") signed the "[Declaration by United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Declaration_by_United_Nations "Declaration by United Nations")",[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-21) and the next day the representatives of twenty-two other nations added their signatures. During the war, the United Nations became the official term for the Allies. In order to join, countries had to sign the Declaration and declare war on the [Axis powers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axis_powers "Axis powers").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-FOOTNOTESchlesinger2003-22)

The October 1943 [Moscow Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow_Conference_(1943) "Moscow Conference (1943)") resulted in the [Moscow Declarations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow_Declarations "Moscow Declarations"), including the [Four Power Declaration on General Security](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Declaration_of_the_Four_Nations "Declaration of the Four Nations"). This declaration was signed by the [Allied Big Four](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Four_(World_War_II) "Big Four (World War II)")—the United States, the Soviet Union, the United Kingdom, and China—and aimed for the creation "at the earliest possible date of a general international organization". This was the first public announcement that a new international organization was being contemplated to replace the League of Nations. The [Tehran Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tehran_Conference "Tehran Conference") followed shortly afterwards at which Roosevelt, Churchill and [Joseph Stalin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Stalin "Joseph Stalin"), the leader of the Soviet Union, met and discussed the idea of a post-war international organization.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-23)

The new international organization was formulated and negotiated amongst the delegations from the [Allied Big Four](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Four_(World_War_II) "Big Four (World War II)") at the [Dumbarton Oaks Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dumbarton_Oaks_Conference "Dumbarton Oaks Conference") from 21 September to 7 October 1944. They agreed on proposals for the aims, structure and functioning of the new organization.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-Bohlen_1973-24)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-25)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-26) It took the [conference at Yalta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yalta_Conference "Yalta Conference") in February 1945, and further negotiations with the Soviet Union, before all the issues were resolved.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-Bohlen_1973-24)

### Founding (1945)

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3a/United_Nations_Member_States-1945.png/500px-United_Nations_Member_States-1945.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:United_Nations_Member_States-1945.png)

The UN in 1945: founding members in light blue, protectorates and territories of the founding members in dark blue (Some nations' land would be different from now.)

By 1 March 1945, 21 additional states had signed the Declaration by the United Nations.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-FOOTNOTEOsma%C5%84czyk20042445-27) After months of planning, the [UN Conference on International Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Conference_on_International_Organization "United Nations Conference on International Organization") opened in [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco") on 25 April 1945. It was attended by 50 nations' governments and a number of non-governmental organizations.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-Charter-28)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-UNHistory-29)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-30) The delegations of the Big Four chaired the plenary meetings.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-31) Previously, Churchill had urged Roosevelt to restore France to its status of a major power after the [liberation of Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberation_of_Paris "Liberation of Paris") in August 1944. The drafting of the [Charter of the United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charter_of_the_United_Nations "Charter of the United Nations") was completed over the following two months, and it was signed on 26 June 1945 by the representatives of the 50 countries.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-32)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-33) The UN officially came into existence at 20:07 ([UTC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coordinated_Universal_Time "Coordinated Universal Time")) on 24 October 1945,[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-34)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-35) upon ratification of the Charter by the five permanent members of the [Security Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council "United Nations Security Council"): the United States, the United Kingdom, France, the Soviet Union and [China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_China_(1912%E2%80%931949) "Republic of China (1912–1949)") — and by a majority of the other 46 nations.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-unmilestones1941to1950-36)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-original_draft-37)

The [first meetings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_session_of_the_United_Nations_General_Assembly "First session of the United Nations General Assembly") of the [General Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Assembly "General Assembly"), with 51 nations represented,[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-40) and the Security Council took place in London beginning in January 1946.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-unmilestones1941to1950-36) Debates began at once, covering topical issues such as the presence of Soviet troops in [Iranian Azerbaijan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iranian_Azerbaijan "Iranian Azerbaijan") and British forces in [Greece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greece "Greece").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-41) British diplomat [Gladwyn Jebb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gladwyn_Jebb "Gladwyn Jebb") served as interim secretary-general.

The General Assembly selected New York City as the site for the headquarters of the UN. Construction began on 14 September 1948 and the facility was completed on 9 October 1952. The Norwegian Foreign Minister, [Trygve Lie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trygve_Lie "Trygve Lie"), was the first elected [UN secretary-general](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary-General_of_the_United_Nations "Secretary-General of the United Nations").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-unmilestones1941to1950-36)

### Cold War (1947–1991)

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f1/Dag_Hammarskj%C3%B6ld_%283x4_cropped%29.jpg/250px-Dag_Hammarskj%C3%B6ld_%283x4_cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dag_Hammarskj%C3%B6ld_(3x4_cropped).jpg)

[Dag Hammarskjöld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dag_Hammarskj%C3%B6ld "Dag Hammarskjöld") was a particularly active secretary-general from 1953 until his death in 1961.

Though the UN's primary mandate was [peacekeeping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peacekeeping "Peacekeeping"), the division between the United States and the Soviet Union often paralysed the organization; this generally allowed it to intervene only in conflicts distant from the [Cold War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War "Cold War").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMeisler199535-42) Two notable exceptions were a Security Council resolution on 7 July 1950 authorizing a [US-led coalition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Command "United Nations Command") to repel the [North Korean invasion of South Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Pokpung "Operation Pokpung"), passed in the absence of the Soviet Union,[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-unmilestones1941to1950-36)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMeisler199558%E2%80%9359-43) and the signing of the [Korean Armistice Agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_Armistice_Agreement "Korean Armistice Agreement") on 27 July 1953.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-44)

On 29 November 1947, the General Assembly approved [Resolution 181](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Partition_Plan_for_Palestine "United Nations Partition Plan for Palestine"), a proposal to partition British Mandatory [Palestine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandatory_Palestine "Mandatory Palestine") into two states, a Jewish state and an Arab state, with Jerusalem placed under international status.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-45) The Partition plan passed 33–13 with 10 abstentions and one absent. The plan was accepted by the Jews and rejected by the Arabs of Palestine and the Arab states [[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations#cite_note-186-20240719-46) leading to [civil war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1947%E2%80%931948_civil_war_in_Mandatory_Palestine "1947–1948 civil war in Mandatory Palestine"). This **list of countries and territories by life expectancy** provides a comprehensive list of countries alongside their respective [life expectancy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_expectancy "Life expectancy") figures. The data are differentiated by sex, presenting life expectancies for males, females, and a combined average. In addition to sovereign nations, the list encompasses several non-sovereign entities and territories. The figures serve as an indicator of the quality of [healthcare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Healthcare "Healthcare") in the respective countries and are influenced by various factors, including the prevalence of diseases such as [HIV/AIDS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HIV/AIDS "HIV/AIDS").

This article introduces the concept of [Healthy life expectancy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Healthy_life_expectancy "Healthy life expectancy") (HALE), which denotes the average number of years a person is expected to live in "full health". There are challenges in comparing life expectancies across countries due to disparities in data reporting and collection standards. The primary source of the most recent data presented is the [World Bank Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Bank_Group "World Bank Group")'s 2022 report.

## Methodology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_countries_by_life_expectancy&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Methodology")]

The [life expectancy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_expectancy "Life expectancy") is shown separately for males and for females, as well as a combined figure. Several non-[sovereign entities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sovereign_state "Sovereign state") and [territories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Territories "Territories") are also included in this list.

The figures reflect the quality of [healthcare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Healthcare "Healthcare") in the countries listed, as well as other factors including [HIV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HIV "HIV") infections.

From the start of the 21st century, estimates of [healthy life expectancy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_expectancy#Healthy_life_expectancy "Life expectancy") (HALE), the average number of years that a person can expect to live in "full health", are also produced.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_life_expectancy#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_life_expectancy#cite_note-4)

Comparing life expectancies across countries can be difficult, due to poor reporting in some countries and different local standards in collecting statistics. This is especially true for healthy life expectancy, the definition of which may change over time, even within a country.

## United Nations (2023)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_countries_by_life_expectancy&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: United Nations (2023)")]

Estimations are by the [United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Department_of_Economic_and_Social_Affairs "United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_life_expectancy#cite_note-un_prospects-5) Only countries with populations over 50,000 are listed. Due to this criterion, the table does not include such countries as [Monaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monaco "Monaco") (LE [86.37 years](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_European_countries_by_life_expectancy#United_Nations_(2023) "List of European countries by life expectancy"), population 39,000), [San Marino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Marino "San Marino") (LE [85.71 years](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_European_countries_by_life_expectancy#United_Nations_(2023) "List of European countries by life expectancy"), population 34,000), and [Saint Barthélemy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Barth%C3%A9lemy "Saint Barthélemy") (LE [84.29 years](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_North_American_countries_by_life_expectancy#United_Nations_(2023) "List of North American countries by life expectancy"), population 11,000). The values are rounded. All calculations were made with raw data.

These values are used to calculate the [Human Development Index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_Development_Index "Human Development Index").

This **list of countries and territories by life expectancy** provides a comprehensive list of countries alongside their respective [life expectancy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_expectancy "Life expectancy") figures. The data are differentiated by sex, presenting life expectancies for males, females, and a combined average. In addition to sovereign nations, the list encompasses several non-sovereign entities and territories. The figures serve as an indicator of the quality of [healthcare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Healthcare "Healthcare") in the respective countries and are influenced by various factors, including the prevalence of diseases such as [HIV/AIDS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HIV/AIDS "HIV/AIDS").

This article introduces the concept of [Healthy life expectancy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Healthy_life_expectancy "Healthy life expectancy") (HALE), which denotes the average number of years a person is expected to live in "full health". There are challenges in comparing life expectancies across countries due to disparities in data reporting and collection standards. The primary source of the most recent data presented is the [World Bank Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Bank_Group "World Bank Group")'s 2022 report.

## Methodology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_countries_by_life_expectancy&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Methodology")]

The [life expectancy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_expectancy "Life expectancy") is shown separately for males and for females, as well as a combined figure. Several non-[sovereign entities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sovereign_state "Sovereign state") and [territories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Territories "Territories") are also included in this list.

The figures reflect the quality of [healthcare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Healthcare "Healthcare") in the countries listed, as well as other factors including [HIV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HIV "HIV") infections.

From the start of the 21st century, estimates of [healthy life expectancy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_expectancy#Healthy_life_expectancy "Life expectancy") (HALE), the average number of years that a person can expect to live in "full health", are also produced.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_life_expectancy#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_life_expectancy#cite_note-4)

Comparing life expectancies across countries can be difficult, due to poor reporting in some countries and different local standards in collecting statistics. This is especially true for healthy life expectancy, the definition of which may change over time, even within a country.

## United Nations (2023)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_countries_by_life_expectancy&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: United Nations (2023)")]

Estimations are by the [United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Department_of_Economic_and_Social_Affairs "United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_life_expectancy#cite_note-un_prospects-5) Only countries with populations over 50,000 are listed. Due to this criterion, the table does not include such countries as [Monaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monaco "Monaco") (LE [86.37 years](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_European_countries_by_life_expectancy#United_Nations_(2023) "List of European countries by life expectancy"), population 39,000), [San Marino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Marino "San Marino") (LE [85.71 years](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_European_countries_by_life_expectancy#United_Nations_(2023) "List of European countries by life expectancy"), population 34,000), and [Saint Barthélemy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Barth%C3%A9lemy "Saint Barthélemy") (LE [84.29 years](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_North_American_countries_by_life_expectancy#United_Nations_(2023) "List of North American countries by life expectancy"), population 11,000). The values are rounded. All calculations were made with raw data.

These values are used to calculate the [Human Development Index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_Development_Index "Human Development Index").
